A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on mixing graph-derived clustering configurations for downstream prediction. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial methodological and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression and classification experiments in Tables 1–2, configuration-count ablations, register-token comparisons, and synthetic clustering analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results across four domains, component and mixing-strategy ablations, low-data experiments, and supplementary inference and predictor analyses.

M1.justification: GraMixC's positional/register-token attention fusion and anchor-based RMS alignment are replaced by MixConfig's MLP selector using sample context, cluster embeddings, and energy/stability statistics, followed by softmax-weighted mixing. v2 handles configuration counts through truncation/padding, adds an inductive nearest-cluster fallback, and introduces surrogate-based selector training for tree predictors. These are procedural changes beyond renaming.

E1.justification: v1's DSNI-pH/temperature, Boston Housing, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Salinas evaluations disappear. v2 evaluates OpenML-CC18, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, MolHIV, BBBP, BACE, SST-2, AG News, and additional UCI datasets. QM9 remains, and the Moons/Blobs example moves from Appendix A to Appendix H. Coverage expands substantially, including a new text domain.

E2.justification: v2 adds DeepCluster-style feature baselines, downstream HDBSCAN comparisons, Fixed-k/Best-cut, and CSPA consensus controls, alongside modality-specific pretrained-model pipelines. HDBSCAN already appeared in v1's synthetic clustering grid; its downstream comparison role is new. RF, XGBoost, and MLP families remain, while CatBoost, TabNet, TabTransformer, PCA/UMAP/autoencoder, and register-token comparisons are removed.

E3.justification: The reported graph degree changes from log10(N) to ceil(log2(n)), with cosine similarity introduced for embedding features. The default MLP changes from hidden sizes [256,128,64] to [128,64]. v2 introduces frozen-embedding/probe evaluations, BBBP five-fold CV, early stopping, a 20% selector-training holdout for tree predictors, and experiments varying training fractions and test-batch sizes.

E4.justification: v1's DSNI count ablation, register analyses, synthetic clustering comparison grid, and MNIST embedding analysis are removed. v2 adds energy/context/cluster-embedding ablations, random/uniform/global mixing and capacity controls, low-data curves, batch-size and permutation tests, and nonlinear-probe and surrogate analyses. The retained Moons/Blobs illustration is relocated evidence, not a new analysis.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports mean ± std over an unspecified number of random seeds, without formal significance testing. v2 specifies five seeds, identifies them as 0–4, and adds paired t-tests and Cohen's d for the main comparisons, plus uncertainty bands for low-data curves. This substantially expands statistical reporting without establishing that run counts increased over v1.

E6.justification: Most result entries are replaced. v1's DSNI results, including FT-Transformer+GMC pH R2 of 0.984, disappear. New v2 results include CIFAR-100 accuracy of 0.742 for Base versus 0.758 for MixConfig and ImageNet-1K accuracy of 0.763 versus 0.782. QM9 uses a different DimeNet++ embedding/head setting, preventing direct version-to-version performance comparison; its new Config and MixConfig entries both report 0.0106 MAE.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the formal CMP objective, predictor-class relationships, Proposition 3.4 on expressiveness, and Remark 4.1 on sample complexity. The reported Hamiltonian repulsion term changes from a sum of squared edge weights to squared clusterwise weight sums. v1's RMS score and two-walk Laplacian mathematics are removed. These exceed restating the retained configuration framework.

C1.justification: The headline contributions shift from three configuration/register properties, novel RMS alignment, and state-of-the-art cultivation-media prediction to a claimed first CMP formulation, energy-aware selection, general compatibility with frozen embeddings and predictors, and gains across four domains and low-data regimes. The broader claim that adaptive configuration mixing benefits prediction remains.

C2.justification: v2 develops new explanations involving energy statistics as inductive bias, sample-specific resolution preferences, and structural regularization under scarce labels. Sections 4.5–5 add applicability limits involving small test batches, single-scale or unclustered data, poor embeddings, and offline extraction preventing joint optimization. v1's register-redundancy interpretation and Boston Housing failure discussion disappear with their associated experiments.

D1.justification: v1's DSNI preprocessing instructions and RMS pseudocode are removed. v2 adds selector dimensions, tree hyperparameters, surrogate-training details, embedding/head interfaces, runtime estimates, and an approximately 200 GPU-hour budget. The reported environment changes from Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6 on RTX 3090 Ti to Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.1 on A100 hardware. v2 also announces and links released source code; its availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially reframes positioning around fixed-resolution clustering, hierarchical methods, and fixed multiresolution representations. It adds substantive comparisons with Matryoshka representations, mixture-of-experts, and cluster ensembles. Much of v1's infant-cognition, microbiome, register, and alignment literature disappears. DINO is positioned as a complementary upstream representation method rather than principally a register-token comparison.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, methodology, experiments, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Preliminary register experiments give way to dedicated Related Work and formal Methods sections; Discussion and Impact Statement sections are added, and the appendices are reorganized. GraMixC becomes MixConfig, CMP terminology is introduced throughout, and author/affiliation information changes.

P2.justification: The main text adopts a two-column conference layout, and the workflow is redrawn around the new selector. RMS/register diagrams, DSNI prediction plots, MNIST embeddings, and the synthetic comparison grid are removed; new low-data curves, a selector-weight heatmap, interface diagrams, and numerous experimental tables replace them. v1 Figure 9 is retained at reduced size as v2 Figure 5 in Appendix H.

improvement.justification: v2 adds valuable component/capacity controls, inference-failure analyses, statistical tests, and implementation information. However, removing RMS leaves correspondence between independently labeled test clusters and learned cluster embeddings unspecified in Sections 3.3.1–3.3.2. CIFAR-100 linear results also differ between Tables 7 (0.742/0.758) and 9 (0.523/0.598) without a clear setting distinction despite Appendix B's common-interface description. These issues affect core inference and experimental traceability, making the net quality direction uncertain despite substantial benefits.
